headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors if Open WebUI feeds Plano outputs into shared tools or files; data leakage is also plausible via broad egress and shared artifacts.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui explicitly supports MCP, plugins, OpenAPI tool servers, and file inputs, while plano exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint with broad egress. If open-webui forwards plano output into tools or shared files, attacker-controlled content can be treated as instructions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF open-webui routes plano responses into MCP/OpenAPI tools without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF either agent renders the other's text as trusted instructions, prompt injection can propagate.
mitigations: Disable tool execution on untrusted model output.
Add provenance labels to all inter-agent messages.
Restrict open-webui to read-only prompts for plano.
Use a separate workspace for each agent.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping middleware.

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui touches files, documents, notes, calendar events, persistent memory, and API keys, and can call cloud APIs; plano touches logs, traces, and metrics and has broad egress. A shared workspace or forwarded context could leak sensitive data from open-webui into plano outputs or external services. The pairwise path is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or mounted volume, sensitive open-webui artifacts can be read by plano.
IF open-webui sends file contents or secrets into external APIs, those contents can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces.
Remove secrets from any shared directory.
Disable file upload for sensitive projects.
Review outbound API destinations for both agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: open-webui can write local files and use mounted volumes, while plano only exposes a config file and does not request elevated privileges or multiple instances. There is some overlap on shared mutable resources if co-located, but the conflict surface is limited and no strong write-write contention is documented.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same directory, file contention can occur.
IF open-webui and plano share a mutable config or volume, last-writer-wins conflicts are possible.
mitigations: Give each agent its own directory.
Mount shared data read-only.
Avoid concurrent edits to config files.
Use file locks for any shared artifact.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can act as a tool-using front end, and plano is an OpenAI-compatible gateway/proxy. If open-webui treats plano output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream tool calls or user-facing actions. This pathway is plausible from the profiles, though not directly observed, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF open-webui uses plano output without verification, incorrect facts can be amplified.
IF plano routes responses from another model into open-webui tool chains, downstream actions may be based on unverified content.
mitigations: Require human review before actions.
Add a verification step before tool calls.
Limit open-webui to non-actionable outputs.
Log and sample inter-agent handoffs.
requires-engineering: implement confidence-based gating.

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui handles API keys, documents, calendar events, and persistent memory, while plano handles logs, traces, and metrics. If regulated or sensitive data flows from open-webui into plano's telemetry or external egress, retention and residency obligations can diverge. No specific certification mismatch is documented, so this is a policy-risk inference.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through plano logs or metrics, retention obligations may be violated.
IF open-webui secrets are forwarded into plano telemetry, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Exclude sensitive fields from logs.
Disable telemetry for regulated workloads.
Keep regulated data out of shared pipelines.
Review retention settings for both systems.
requires-engineering: add policy-based redaction and residency controls.
